name: Browser Agent Ecosystem
description: Bring-your-own browser stack. Twenty-six vendor adapters over one audited path, a declared activity-destination catalog, buyer-declared origin allowlists, and read-only execution. The buyer supplies the browser vendor account, the transport, the credential vault, and the destination their activity records go to.
_minModules: The buyer graph must reach the whole portable: the barrel, twenty-six adapters, the shared kit, the port definitions, the vendor catalog, the activity-sink catalog and the test doubles. A shorter walk means an adapter or a port stopped being reachable from an entry point, which is how a vendor silently leaves the product.
_hostFallbacks: Bare or aliased specifiers reached by the buyer graph but supplied by the buyer. Keep empty. This portable reached FOUR external things in July and every one of them was removed rather than declared: a Supabase SDK, two modules in lib/browser-runtime, and one type from lib/browser-provider.
buyerMustSupply: A browser vendor account, or a grid, fleet or engine they run themselves — twenty-six adapters are pre-staged; none of the accounts are.
RemoteAdapterTransport — performs the vendor call. The buyer holds the account, so the vendor request is theirs by design.
RemoteAdapterCredentialBroker — resolves a credential from their vault per launch. Optional for the three vendors whose catalog contract says a credential is not required.
Approved origins — a non-empty allowlist of exact origins. Nothing outside it is reachable.
An activity destination — one of eleven pre-staged, or their own declaration. Requires their http.send or sql.execute primitive.
Approval, policy, evidence, telemetry, scheduler and human-control ports, per their own governance.
notIncluded: Any browser vendor account, subscription or credential.
A browser engine, a driver, an HTTP client or a database driver. The payload has no runtime dependency at all.
execute_change execution. Every adapter refuses it; this release observes and prepares only.
A hosted database, vault, network transport or SIEM.
Playwright and Puppeteer as REMOTE adapters — they are local engines, served by the local adapter rather than the remote kit.
supportedPlatforms: Buyer-selected vendor, vault, network and persistence implementations
Linux and macOS build hosts; no native modules

upgradeCompatibility.policy: Within 1.x the buyer-facing interfaces are additive only. New vendor adapters are additions, never a break.
upgradeCompatibility.ledgerSchema: The payload owns no datastore schema. Activity destinations write into the buyer's own table or endpoint.
upgradeCompatibility.rollback: The payload holds no state and can be replaced by restoring the previous verified archive.

knownLimitations: The release candidate validates packaging and integrity only; it is not evidence of buyer deployment acceptance.

Twenty-six adapters are CONFIGURATION AND GOVERNANCE around a call the buyer implements. The vendor HTTP request itself is theirs, deliberately — inventing twenty-six vendor protocols we could not verify would be worse than asking for a transport.
One catalog vendor of twenty-seven has no remote adapter: the Playwright/Puppeteer local-engine pair, already covered by the local adapter.
execute_change is disabled for every vendor in this release.

acceptance.how: Import the entry point in a clean buyer environment and call runBrowserAcceptance({ adapterId, buildSessionFactory, configuration, transport, credentialBroker, probeOrigin }) with the factory builder for whichever of the twenty-six vendors the buyer owns, their own transport and vault broker, and an https origin they control. Fourteen checks are reported independently; nine of them assert a REFUSAL. Pass an optional `activity` block to also prove records reach the destination they chose.
acceptance.guarantee: The payload contains no credential and no vendor account, refuses execute_change on every adapter, reaches no network destination it chose itself, and passes every failure through a sanitizer that strips live credentials from error text.
acceptance.evidence: The returned browser-agent-acceptance/1 record is the acceptance artifact. Retain it; it names which properties held, against which vendor and which probe origin.
